note: Jel phonotactic rules + root lexicon. 'provenance' on each root: community-data = gloss reported by a community wiki summary (2nd-hand, see RI-LOR01 provenance); inferred = our decomposition of a canon proper noun; constructed = our invention. NEVER present 'constructed' roots as canon Jel.

consonant_notes.x: voiceless velar fricative /x/, never /ks/ — the signature sound of Jel
consonant_notes.ts: affricate, valid as onset and coda

phonology.stress: penultimate syllable of each element; in a hyphenated compound, primary stress falls on the final element

forbidden.note_on_apostrophe: APOSTROPHES ARE FORBIDDEN IN JEL. They belong to Khajiit (J'zhirr, Ra'dashi) and rarely Redguard. An apostrophe in an Argonian proper noun is an automatic validator failure and is the single most common way a fantasy language reads as random typing.
forbidden.note_on_f_q_y: Jel has no /f/, no /q/, and no consonantal /j/ spelled y. 'y' is not used at all.
forbidden.note_on_doubles: No geminate spellings (nn, ll, tt, ss, kk, mm, rr). 'thth' is permitted medially only, as in Thitithil.

phonology.attested_exceptions_note: Canon or loaned forms that predate our rules and are exempt from phonotactic validation. They are exceptions BECAUSE they are attested; nothing new may be coined on their pattern. 'kaoc' is the only Jel item containing 'c'.

suffixes.gloss: one who does, one who passes on

reduplication.rule: Partial reduplication of a root marks repetition, intensity, or plurality of the OBJECT, not the actor.

compounding.hyphenation: Hyphenate when 2+ elements and any element is 2+ syllables (Ixtaxh-Thitithil-Meht). Fuse when both elements are monosyllabic (xanmeer, wuxal).

coined_terms.meaning: The soul-residue a killer carries. The game's souls currency.
A Hist root deliberately cut and kept open. Bonfire analogue.
Stoppered gourd of sapwell sap. Estus analogue.
The grey fungal knot that grows where you dropped your tithe. Bloodstain analogue.
What a non-Argonian accrues by using sapwells. Rests on CF-006.
Soul-trapping into gems. The great Argonian obscenity.
Trees or wells that have stopped answering.
Interior isolationist consensus out of Helstrom. Faction.
Heretics who cut wells for profit. Faction.

tamrielic_name_grammar.gender_marking: His/Her in the determiner slot marks gender (canon: Lifts-Her-Tail, Hides-His-Eyes). Absence marks nothing.
tamrielic_name_grammar.register_rule: A Tamrielic Argonian name should read as something an adult once said ABOUT a hatchling, or as the thing that person is known for doing badly. It is never a title earned in battle.
tamrielic_name_grammar.blocklist_note: Any hyphenated Argonian name containing a blocklist noun is an automatic fail. 'Slays-The-Shadow-Lord' is the exact failure this list exists to catch. Exception: a registered in-fiction epithet deliberately mocking the register.

imperial.structure: praenomen + nomen; officers and scholars add a cognomen or a post ('formerly Quartermaster of the Ninth Cohort')

dunmer.structure: given name + family/House name; honorific Serjo (noble) or Sera (polite) precedes
houses_present_in_black_marsh: Telvanni (individual mages, soul-gem trade — see xul-hesh)

khajiit.structure: honorific prefix + name; the prefix encodes standing
khajiit.apostrophe_rule: Khajiit are the ONLY culture in our world permitted apostrophes (rare Redguard 'at-' constructions excepted). This is what makes the apostrophe meaningful rather than decorative.
khajiit.speech_note: Khajiit traders refer to themselves in the third person; this is a speech convention, not a naming one.

kothringi.status: constructed — canon gives the people (CF-047) but no name corpus
kothringi.structure: single given name, two syllables, soft onsets, Nedic-flavoured
kothringi.distinguishing_rule: Must not read as Breton (no -ien, -ard, -aud) and must not read as Nord (no -gar, -olf, -ulf). Silver-toned, plain, slightly archaic.
kothringi.note: Found only on graves, ruins, ship registers, and one impossible living person (CF-049).
